mechanism_narrative: The current level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. Higher FEDFUNDS levels compress equity valuations by increasing discount rates, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negatively correlated with FEDFUNDS levels (Spearman rank correlation < -0.15) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy cycle, which increases the risk-free rate and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances (or rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains below 4.5%, it signals a strong labor market and accommodative monetary policy, which supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy with strong labor market
failure_condition: In instances where UNRATE < 4.5% and FEDFUNDS < 4.5%, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (or rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: In strong consumer demand cycles (HOUST > 1900 and RSAFS > 360000), the S&P 500 exhibits positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to sustained earnings growth from robust consumer spending.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST > 1900 and RSAFS > 360000, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases (or rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which increases the risk of recession and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances (or rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 110 (2017=100) signals a contraction in the real economy, which increases the probability of recession and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 110, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases (or rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 110 and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a policy response to economic weakness, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary policy response to economic weakness
failure_condition: In instances where INDPRO < 110 and FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases (or rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1900 signals a weakening housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 1900, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases (or rank IC < 0.05).
